barangayIntegration.inventoryObservation: Get Involved currently initializes type, tool and subject from query parameters but does not initialize its barangay field from the barangay query parameter. The barangay value passed by /participate is therefore not automatically prefilled.

crossSiteParticipationEntrypoints: PageHelp correction CTA on most pages

existing: scripts/check-civic-map.mjs validates major Civic Map content/methodology assumptions.
Critical-path browser tests cover Civic Map consolidated reports, failed-feed behavior, barangay homepage → scoped Civic Map, and national infrastructure handoffs.
page-audit.json tracks /participate as reviewed and /civic-map as partial.
coverageGaps: /get-involved is not currently listed in page-audit.json.
/civic-map/reports is not currently listed in page-audit.json.
/contact is not currently listed in page-audit.json.
No dedicated participation-depth audit currently covers the whole participation journey.
Existing critical-path tests do not constitute a complete end-to-end POST submission/lifecycle test suite.

observationsFor3A2.observation: A barangay query parameter can be generated upstream, but Get Involved does not read it into the initial form state.
Several participation surfaces are functional but absent from the human page-audit inventory.
The implementation supports many asset and issue types, but the current seed map contains only six assets concentrated in Poblacion plus one Ayala Avenue segment spanning San Lorenzo / Bel-Air.
Lifecycle recording is implemented, but referral delivery remains a human-reviewed process rather than automatic government forwarding.
The participation data currently has no open official participation opportunity and explicitly records the absence of a complete authoritative citywide consultation calendar.
page-audit.json records that response time and participation conversion are not yet measured longitudinally.

General project feedback uses /api/feedback while public-realm reports/proposals/ratings use /api/civic. 3A-2 should decide whether the visible distinction is clear enough, without merging unlike workflows merely for architectural neatness.
